comparison: iPhone13,1 iOS 27.0.1 (24A446) vs iOS 27.2 (24B119), targeted follow-up

functions.name: ipc_is_valid_exception_port
functions.observation: The 27.2 function adds a second entitlement query for com.apple.security.cs.debugger after the existing com.apple.private.set-exception-port query. Both queries use a 30-instruction helper that is shape-identical between builds (old 0xfffffff00a97d030, new 0xfffffff00a9bd5cc, shape SHA-256 bc492fb823add45c...).

functions.name: set_exception_ports_validation
functions.observation: The 27.2 function adds a com.apple.security.cs.debugger entitlement query alongside the existing com.apple.private.set-exception-port query before proceeding. The later com.apple.security.only-one-exception-port check is retained.

exception_port_validation.interpretation: Both exception-port validation paths accept an additional debugger entitlement in 27.2. This is an observed behavior change, not evidence of a vulnerability fix; it broadens rather than narrows the accepted entitlement set.

ghidra_decompilation.method: Ghidra headless analyzer with auto-analysis, then DecompileFuncs post-script

observed_differences: 24B119 queries com.apple.security.cs.debugger in addition to com.apple.private.thread-set-state in three access-check paths; 24A446 queries only com.apple.private.thread-set-state.
The combined branch denies in the path where both entitlement queries succeed; because the helper return convention is inferred from its use, the net authorization effect is not established.
24B119 adds a leading call to an unidentified policy routine at 0xfffffff00aa1aedc when bit 0 of the flag argument is set; a nonzero result returns 8.

The IPC policy-violation denial path is routed through a wrapper at 0xfffffff00a1b8958 in 24B119; 24A446 calls ipc_triage_policy_violation directly. No semantic conclusion is drawn from this refactor.
thread_state_validation.interpretation: 24B119 adds a debugger-entitlement query to the thread-state path. The combined branch structure makes the net authorization effect unclear; it is an observed behavior change, not evidence of a vulnerability fix.

one_sided_name.note: Includes slot reordering: four method names appear at different slots in the two builds.

same_slot_different_name.note: All at inherited slot 71 across 16 classes; the new target is named PMSettingObject::pmSettingObject, but its disassembly matches IOUserClient::sendAsyncResult. This is a symbolicator misattribution or inherited-slot alignment issue, not evidence of 16 method replacements.

symbol_map_warning.actual_match: The disassembly matches 27.0 IOUserClient::sendAsyncResult at 0xfffffff00a8a6888; the 27.2 symbol map does not contain sendAsyncResult.
symbol_map_warning.implication: Symbolicator labels are candidate labels only; at least one label is demonstrably wrong.

ane_vtable_qualification.interpretation: The raw 55-slot count overstates method-level change because it compares by slot index and includes inherited-slot and symbol-name effects. The name-aware subset is 7 unique changed-body target pairs, with 11 one-sided and 16 unnamed pairs unresolved.

functions.name: vm_map_remap
observed_changes: 24B119 rejects the request when flag bit 8 is set and (flag bit 43 is set, or *param_9 > 1, or *param_10 > 1).
24B119 clears bits 7 and 16 of a VM entry's flag word (mask 0xfffeff7f) when flag bit 8 is set and entry bit 7 is set.
The pmap_create_options_internal path and several object field offsets differ; their semantics were not established.
functions.status: observed code change; no CVE mapping

functions.name: vm_object_update
observed_changes: 24B119 increments a 32-bit counter at object byte offset 0xe8 when the pl_req path is taken and panics on overflow (vm_object_pl_req_begin).
24B119 decrements the same counter on exit, panics on underflow (vm_object_pl_req_end), and clears bit 0 of object byte offset 0x74 when the counter reaches zero.
The existing vm_object_paging_begin/end accounting is retained; several call targets and field offsets differ because of the build change.
functions.status: observed code change; no CVE mapping

advisory_context.status: The 27.2 advisory lists 15 Kernel CVEs covering use-after-free, out-of-bounds, type-confusion, race, memory-integrity, and information-disclosure issues. The two VM changes are temporal and functional candidates only; no routine is mapped to a CVE.

kernel_structural_followup.interpretation: The decompilation narrows two of the 222 structural kernel candidates to concrete validation and accounting changes. Neither change is proven to be a security fix, and neither is mapped to an advisory entry.

limitations: No source-level semantics, call-graph equivalence, or CVE attribution is established.
The extracted kernel and kext images are stripped; symbolicator labels are partial and can be wrong.
Same virtual addresses across builds are not function correspondence; the AVE2 old/new pairs are recorded only as same-VA context.
Vtable slot comparison by index is affected by inherited slots, slot reordering, and parser alignment; counts are not a method-change count.
No device was connected; runtime behavior and exploitability were not measured.
The new AVE2 checks are described only by their range-check structure; no specific CVE is mapped to a routine.
thread_set_state_internal, vm_map_remap, and vm_object_update are paired by symbolicator name; source-level equivalence is not established.
The vm_map_remap flag bits and vm_object_update field offsets are decompiler-derived and were not checked against kernel source.
The vm_object_pl_req_begin/end counter is an observed accounting change; its purpose and security relevance are not established.
